title: AEPRecord
description: Agent Evidence Protocol record — runtime action evidence and run provenance. Canonical source for wasmagent-js, wasmagent-proxy, trace-pipeline, wasmagent-train-replay, and open-agent-audit.

user_id.description: Optional end-user / principal the run acted on behalf of (additive, aep/v0.3+).

subject_id.description: Optional agent subject identity for the run (additive, aep/v0.3+).

authorized_by.description: Principal that granted or approved the authority this run exercised, when that party differs from user_id (additive, aep/v0.5+). Distinguishes the party who initiated from the party who authorized; omit when the same principal did both. Per-action human-approval evidence continues to live in actions[].approval_context_hash.

authority_origin.description: How the principal named in user_id obtained the authority this run exercised, as observable at issuance/consent time (additive, aep/v0.5+). Authority origin axis of the attribution vocabulary shared with the OWASP 'Verifiable Authorization Lineage' recommended control. subject_consented = the principal interactively approved; administrator_assigned = an administrator created the grant and no principal was ever prompted; organization_wide = consent granted on behalf of an organization. unknown = the producer observed the attribution but the identity provider does not expose grant origin — the honest state for most current IdPs, and the value that stops a consumer reading user_id as stronger evidence than it is. Absent = the producer makes no claim. Motivating case (OWASP www-project-mcp-top-10 #44/#50): two grants byte-identical in every identity claim, one subject-consented and one administrator-assigned — user_id alone cannot separate them; this field can.

identity_source.description: How the identity behind the backing key was established (additive, aep/v0.5+). Identity source axis of the attribution vocabulary shared with the OWASP 'Verifiable Authorization Lineage' recommended control, alongside attribution_backing (what stands behind the authorization) and authority_origin (how the authority was conferred). self_asserted = the keyholder asserted their own identity; organization_attested = the organization attests the identity; notified_eid = identity established via a notified electronic identity; qualified_certificate = identity established via a qualified certificate. Reported verbatim alongside the grade — NEVER folded into attribution_backing and never rounded up: a device-key signature by a person whose identity was eID-proofed is still principal_key_signed on the backing axis. unknown = the provider does not expose how the identity was established; absent = the producer makes no claim.

attribution_backing.description: Machine-checkable statement of what backs the human attribution of this record (additive, aep/v0.5+). Attribution backing axis of the attribution vocabulary shared with the OWASP 'Verifiable Authorization Lineage' recommended control. Grades the evidence behind the attribution — operator_asserted = operator assertion only, no signature by a key under the principal's control; principal_key_signed = backed by such a signature; qualified_signature = backed by a qualified identity-proofed signature (e.g. QES validated against an EU Trusted List); unknown = attribution present but ungradeable. NOT a claim that the runtime authorization predicate was correctly constrained, and not a scope statement. Producers MUST NOT report a stronger grade than the evidence supports; where ordering matters (run_attribution_backing_floor) unknown is weaker than operator_asserted.

run_attribution_backing_floor.description: Per-run aggregate: the weakest attribution backing present across the authorizations this run relied on (additive, aep/v0.5+). Shares the attribution_backing vocabulary. Total order, weakest to strongest: unknown < operator_asserted < principal_key_signed < qualified_signature. The floor MUST NOT round up — one strong grant must not mask unbacked authorizations inside the same tamper-evident record. When authorization_evidence_count is present, the floor MUST equal the weakest grade across that declared set. Report together with run_attribution_backing_observed, never instead of it. Absent = the producer emits no attribution_backing values and makes no grading claim at all.

run_attribution_backing_observed.description: Per-run aggregate: every attribution backing grade observed across the authorizations this run relied on (additive, aep/v0.5+). Shares the attribution_backing vocabulary. Reported alongside run_attribution_backing_floor — the floor alone loses the information that a strong authorization exists anywhere in the run; the itemization alone permits exactly the masking the floor exists to prevent.

authorization_evidence_count.description: Number of distinct authorization evidence items the run relied on (additive, aep/v0.5+). Selective-omission defense: without this count, a producer can omit a weak authorization entirely and report only the strong ones — the observed set still looks self-consistent. The count commits the producer to a specific evidence population; an auditor who later discovers the true count differs has a tamper indicator. Absent = the producer makes no completeness claim.

side_effect_class.description: Per-record side-effect classification (additive, aep/v0.3+). Shares one vocabulary with run_side_effect_class_max; reconciles wasmagent-js and trace-pipeline forks.

run_side_effect_class_max.description: Per-run aggregate: the highest side-effect class observed across the whole run (additive, aep/v0.3+). Shares the side_effect_class vocabulary.

recording_mode.description: Retention depth of captured evidence for this run (additive, aep/v0.3+). Controls how much of what was observed the producer chose to keep — NOT a claim about observation scope or coverage. full = complete provenance (all observed data retained); delta = before/after state digests only; validation = action metadata only (minimum retention). A narrow-scope monitor and a wide-scope monitor produce identical recording_mode values; observation scope is a property of the producing monitor's configuration, not of this record.

argument_drift.description: Detected drift between an action's declared arguments and the arguments used at runtime (additive, aep/v0.3+).

dsse_envelope.description: DSSE envelope (aep/v0.4+). Present when the producer signed via DSSE PAE; the legacy signature field is derived from the envelope's signatures[0] for backward compatibility. payload is base64-encoded; payloadType uses DSSE PayloadType format.

signature.description: Optional tamper-evident signature. Stays OPTIONAL in every released schema version (aep/v0.1-v0.5); tightening it to required is a breaking change (CONTRACT-CHANGE-PROCESS.md section 3) that needs an org RFC before it can land - do not silently add it to the 'required' array.
